papers.title: Floquet Engineering of a Quasiequilibrium Superradiant Phase Transition in Landau Polaritons
papers.authors: Wen-Hua Wu, Fuyang Tay, Mengqian Che, Andrey Baydin, Junichiro Kono, David Hagenmüller
papers.abstract: Superradiant phase transitions (SRPTs), characterized by photon condensation and macroscopic matter polarization, are forbidden in equilibrium for homogeneous fields by no-go theorems. Here, we show that Floquet driving can circumvent this constraint in a Landau polariton system consisting of a two-dimensional electron gas coupled to a terahertz cavity in a DC magnetic field. An off-resonant AC magnetic field modulates the cyclotron frequency and light--matter coupling strength while leaving the diamagnetic term unchanged, generating an additional DC coupling contribution. This drives the system across a critical threshold into a superradiant phase, characterized by photon condensation and Landau-level polarization in the ground state of the Floquet Hamiltonian. This quasiequilibrium approach offers a route to SRPTs distinct from driven-dissipative schemes.

papers.title: Probing Bilayer Topological Order with Layer-Resolved Transport
papers.authors: Hongquan Liu, J. I. A. Li, D. E. Feldman
papers.abstract: Shot noise has been used to measure fractional charges of anyons. The value of the charge imposes constraints on fractional statistics but does not determine it. This limitation is particularly important in multi-component systems. For example, the zero charge of neutral anyons in bilayer graphene gives no information about their statistics at all. We propose a way to shed light on the statistics of charged and neutral anyons in multi-component systems with layer-resolved or spin- resolved noise. The protocol applies to the fractional quantum spin Hall effect in MoTe$_2$, topological states in multi-layer graphene and bilayer GaAs, and to recently discovered fractional excitons in bilayer graphene. The approach relies on the relation between statistics and the distribution of the anyon charge over the components. Information about statistics can also be extracted from a simpler measurement of the layer-resolved electric current through a narrow constriction in a Hall bar even in the presence of long-range interactions and other non-universal effects.

papers.title: Tomographic Electron Flow in Confined Geometries: Beyond the Dual-Relaxation-Time Approximation
papers.authors: Nitay Ben-Shachar, Johannes Hofmann
papers.abstract: Hydrodynamiclike electron flows are typically modeled using the Stokes-Ohm equation or a kinetic description that is based on a dual-relaxation-time approximation. Such models assume a short intrinsic mean free path ℓ e due to momentum-conserving electronic scattering and a large extrinsic mean free path ℓ MR due to momentum-relaxing impurity scattering. This assumption, however, is overly simplistic and falls short at low temperatures, where it is known from exact diagonalization studies of the electronic collision integrals that another large electronic mean free path ℓ o emerges that describes long-lived odd electron modes—this is sometimes known as the tomographic effect. Here, using a matched asymptotic expansion of the underlying Fermi-liquid kinetic equation with multiple electron relaxation times, we derive a transport theory for tomographic flows in arbitrary smooth boundary geometries. Our key results are a set of governing equations for the electron density and electron current, their slip boundary conditions (which are applied at diffuse boundaries), and boundary layer corrections near diffuse edges. We find that the tomographic effect strongly modifies previous hydrodynamic theories for electron flows: In particular, (i) a local equilibrium is established in the bulk, where the flow is governed by Stokes-Ohm-like equations with significant finite-wavelength corrections, (ii) the velocity slip condition at the boundary is strongly modified and not accounted for by the widely used hydrodynamic slip-length condition, (iii) a large kinetic boundary layer of width ∼ ℓ e ℓ o arises near diffuse boundaries, which is much larger than in conventional near-hydrodynamic theories, and (iv) all these effects are strongly suppressed by an external magnetic field. We illustrate our findings for electron flow in a channel. The equations derived here provide a comprehensive framework for future studies of tomographic flows in smooth geometries.
papers.summary_en: The authors derive a kinetic theory for tomographic electron flow in smooth confined geometries, showing how long-lived odd modes alter bulk flow, diffuse-boundary slip, and boundary layers relative to standard hydrodynamic models. They also find that an external magnetic field strongly suppresses these effects.

papers.title: Coherence and pairing enhancement in a trilayer cuprate with layer-selective charge order
papers.authors: Steef Smit, Martin Bluschke, Peter C. Moen, Niclas Heinsdorf, Edoardo Zavatti, Gabriele Bellomia, Samuele Giuli, Sydney K. Y. Dufresne, Cissy T. Dadap, Pinder Dosanjh, Marta Zonno, Sergey Gorovikov, Heemin Lee, Cheng-Tai Kuo, Jun-Sik Lee, Dongjoon Song, Shigeyuki Ishida, Hiroshi Eisaki, Bernhard Keimer, Matteo Michiardi, Ilya S. papers.abstract: Trilayer cuprates hold the record for the highest superconducting critical temperatures (Tc), yet the underlying mechanism remains elusive. Using time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (tr-ARPES), we uncover a striking interplay between charge order, superconducting gap magnitude, and quasiparticle coherence in Bi2Sr2Ca2Cu3O10+δ (Bi2223). We present ARPES-based evidence of charge order on the inner CuO2 plane – as confirmed via resonant x-ray scattering (RXS) – and show that the same inner plane hosts a large superconducting gap matching its doping, firmly establishing it as underdoped. Despite its underdoped nature, the inner plane also exhibits an exceptional degree of quasiparticle coherence; suppressing charge-order fluctuations further enhances this, making it comparable to that of the overdoped outer planes at elevated electronic temperatures. At the same time, on the overdoped outer planes we find larger superconducting gaps than what is seen on comparably doped single and bilayer cuprates, indicating an unexpected and simultaneous enhancement of both coherence and pairing interactions in Bi2223. These findings, supported by complementary single- and three-layer Hubbard model calculations, reveal a unique interlayer mechanism in which both pairing strength and phase coherence are optimized when interfacing planes with distinct hole concentrations, providing new microscopic insight into the record Tc of Bi2223. The authors study the electronic structure of cuprate superconductor Bi2Sr2Ca2Cu3O10+δ with three CuO2 planes in the unit cell. They find that proximity coupling of the underdoped inner CuO2 plane to the overdoped outer CuO2 planes simultaneously strengthens pairing and quasiparticle coherence.
papers.summary_en: Using time- and angle-resolved photoemission, the authors investigate how charge order, superconducting gaps, and quasiparticle coherence vary between the inner and outer CuO₂ planes of trilayer Bi2223. They argue that coupling planes with different hole concentrations enhances both pairing and coherence.

papers.title: Deep strong light-matter coupling in 3D Kane fermions without Dicke criticality
papers.authors: Dmitriy Yavorskiy, David Hagenmüller, Noureddine Charrouj, Yurii Ivonyak, Alexander Kazakov, Yanko Todorov, Wojciech Knap, Marcin Białek
papers.abstract: Abstract Deep-strong light-matter coupling is a non-perturbative regime of quantum electrodynamics in which the interaction strength exceeds the frequencies of uncoupled light and matter excitations. Whether a Dicke superradiant phase transition can occur in electronic systems with linear energy-momentum dispersion remains controversial because of the apparent absence of a diamagnetic A 2 term in their low-energy Hamiltonian. Here, we investigate Landau polaritons in a bulk mercury cadmium telluride film hosting Kane fermions coupled to a Fabry-Perot resonator. The ultralow cyclotron mass of Kane fermions and a thermally tunable carrier density enable tuning from weak to deep-strong coupling, reaching the single-mode coupling strength of 1.6 above room temperature. Near the Dirac point (100 K), deep-strong coupling coexists with linear low-energy dispersion. Our microscopic quantum theory and classical electromagnetic simulations are in agreement with measured spectra. We conclude that a diamagnetic A 2 term emerges despite the linear dispersion, preventing a Dicke superradiant phase transition.

papers.abstract: Altermagnets break time-reversal symmetry despite their zero net magnetization, enabling time-reversal-odd responses while retaining the advantages of antiferromagnets. However, magneto-optical (MO) effects are not universal among altermagnets because MO effects typically arise from magnetic dipole order (ferromagnetism), which is generally absent in altermagnets. In this work, we address this limitation by establishing octupolar MO effects, which arise from magnetic octupole order through spatial dispersion. Owing to this distinct origin, octupolar MO effects do not necessarily require spin-orbit coupling even in collinear magnets and can arise without an external magnetic field in antiferromagnets where conventional MO effects are symmetry-forbidden. Such antiferromagnets include $d$-wave altermagnets such as RuO$_2$ and KV$_2$Se$_2$O, certain $g$- and $i$-wave altermagnets, including CrSb, as well as noncoplanar antiferromagnets such as MnTe$_2$ and pyrochlore iridates with all-in-all-out magnetic order. From an experimental perspective, octupolar MO effects can reach detectable magnitudes and offer potential for magnetic-domain imaging, as supported by numerical calculations showing $μ$rad-scale Faraday rotation for a 100-nm-thick sample in the visible-light range and a sign reversal between opposite domains. Furthermore, octupolar MO effects are linked to an $f$-sum rule, enabling a quantitative estimate of the spin magnetic octupole moment from optical measurements. These results extend the scope of MO effects to a broad class of antiferromagnets, including altermagnets, and open a field-free optical route to exploring magnetic octupole order.

papers.abstract: Carrier self-trapping is a fundamental relaxation pathway in strongly correlated quantum materials, yet the microscopic lattice motions that drive it have remained largely inaccessible to direct observation. Here we investigate the van der Waals antiferromagnet NiPS$_3$ upon excitation across its ligand-to-metal charge-transfer gap, and reveal a nonequilibrium pathway that initially generates unbound carriers before they evolve into correlated excitonic states. Using ultrabroadband optical-pump terahertz-probe spectroscopy, we simultaneously track carrier localization and the associated lattice dynamics in real time. Temperature-dependent measurements, together with mode-resolved dielectric dynamics and symmetry analysis, identify the 2.7 and 8.0 THz responses as spectroscopic indicators of exciton self-trapping and point to a cooperative two-phonon mechanism. papers.abstract: In frustrated spin chains with competing nearest- and next-nearest-neighbor exchange, the vector spin chirality sets the electric polarization, so a ferroelectric domain wall is a domain wall of the chirality. The semiclassical picture suggests nonlocal switching dynamics due to topological constraints on the spins, but little is known about such domain walls in a quantum spin chain. Using density-matrix renormalization group calculations for a frustrated spin-1/2 XXZ chain in which a bond alternation $δ$ opens a spin gap, we show that the wall then becomes a quantum particle. In a finite chain, it has the energy levels and wave functions of a particle in a box, and it moves under an electric field as a particle under a constant force does. In the infinite chain, its mass grows by more than two orders of magnitude as $δ$ decreases and diverges at $δ^*\approx0.012$, where the bottom of its band becomes flat; below $δ^*$ the band has two degenerate minima away from its center. The large mass results from a near cancellation of in-plane and out-of-plane exchange energies.

papers.abstract: The layered anti-ferromagnet CrSBr hosts self-hybridized exciton-polaritons that couple parametrically to coherent magnons and phonons. In this work, we explore the tripartite optomechanical interaction between these quasiparticles in suspended CrSBr membranes supporting high-$Q$ breathing-type acoustic phonon modes. Using resonant pump-probe spectroscopy on the polariton state, we resolve the coupled dynamics in the $\simeq 20$ GHz range while sweeping the magnon mode across the phonon resonance with an external magnetic field. We observe an attractive magnon-phonon interaction of strength $V/2π= -43$ MHz, which primarily leads to phonon amplification. At the magnon-phonon resonance, we find predominantly unidirectional energy flow from magnons to phonons while the possible back-action is limited by kinetic losses of coherent magnons. Our study enables direct interfacing of collective magnetic excitations with sound and light in layered van der Waals materials, paving the way for quantum-coherent transduction in the GHz range with optical readout.

papers.abstract: Gauge invariance forbids equilibrium photon condensation for spatially uniform electric-dipole coupling, motivating alternative routes based on orbital magnetic response. We show that triangular molecular magnets coupled to a cavity support photon condensation driven by emergent scalar spin chirality. Starting from the half-filled Hubbard model in the Mott regime, we derive an effective Hamiltonian in which virtual ring exchange couples the cavity flux directly to scalar spin chirality. Our results establish emergent orbital degrees of freedom in frustrated magnets as a route to equilibrium light-matter ordering beyond conventional dipolar cavity quantum electrodynamics.

papers.summary_en: Using neural quantum states, the authors study electrons at Landau-level filling νB = 1 in a moiré potential and find an extended regime where molecular charge order coexists with a quantized Hall response. papers.abstract: Two-dimensional electrons in a strong magnetic field exhibit two seemingly incompatible ground states: incompressible quantum Hall liquids with a quantized Hall conductance, and electron crystals in which interactions drive the charge into ordered patterns. Moiré superlattices in transition-metal-dichalcogenide bilayers offer a tunable arena for this competition. Using neural quantum states (NQS) together with several methodological advances, we show how this competition unfolds. In particular, we demonstrate that the two end points are separated by an extended regime in which molecular charge order coexists with a quantized Hall response. We map the ground-state phase diagram of electrons at Landau-level filling $ν_B=1$ in the presence of a moiré superlattice potential, with three electrons per moiré cell. In the deep triangular potential limit, the electrons form the topologically trivial "Wigner molecular crystal'' of three-electron artificial atoms, a state recently imaged at zero magnetic field in moiré bilayers. As the potential depth is lowered, molecular charge order remains while quantized Hall response emerges. At the honeycomb point, where each cell contains three electrons and two degenerate moiré minima, wells are either singly or doubly occupied and the doublons provide an emergent Ising degree of freedom. Starting from modest interaction strength, we find short-range doublon correlations within the Chern insulator which grow with interaction strength and eventually break sublattice symmetry, forming a Néel CDW with long-range order between doublons. The topological molecular regime lies at twist angles and magnetic fields directly accessible to current experiments. The methodological advances presented provide a scalable framework for exploring a broad range of questions in correlated quantum matter in the presence of magnetic fields.

papers.abstract: Non-Hermitian localization transitions often accompany multiple mobility edges, but their physical origin can be ambiguous. To address the issue, we introduce an extension of the Ganeshan-Pixley-Das Sarma model with both asymmetric hopping and complex onsite potential, thereby incorporating a broad range of non-Hermitian quasiperiodic chains. Its solution reveals two energy-dependent localization contributions manifested as distinct Lyapunov growth scales, whose competition determines the structure of mobility edges. We derive exact Lyapunov exponents via Avila's global theory, obtain thresholds of the two channels on complex-energy plane, and formulate a selection rule that distinguishes physical mobility edges from suppressed analytical candidates. The channel that uniquely controls localization can switch with energy, producing complex mobility edges of non-Hermitian origins. Nonreciprocal hopping further shifts the thresholds and alters the bulk energy patterns. Numerical spectra and finite-size localization diagnostics confirm the theory. Our work thus provides a unified framework for characterizing phase transitions and mobility edges under competing localization mechanisms in non-Hermitian quasicrystals.

papers.abstract: Flexoelectricity (polarization induced by strain gradients) is assumed to be insensitive to space inversion in all materials: flexoelectric polarization should not depend on whether a crystal is bent upwards or downwards. papers.abstract: A persistent mystery of CuO_2-based high temperature superconductivity has been the mechanism and consequences of time reversal ($\mathcal{T}$)-symmetry breaking. Although theoretical hypotheses focus upon persistent electronic currents as a potential cause, these have been invisible to direct experimental probes. That impasse has recently been removed by development of techniques for atomic-scale supercurrent visualization. Here, by imaging the energy-resolved density of electronic states $N(r,E)$ in $\mathrm{Bi_2Sr_2CaCu_2O_8}$, we search for the specific signatures of flowing supercurrents in a disordered $d$-wave superconductor. Employing the strategy of artificial neural networks (ANN) for complex quantum matter visualization, we designed a dual-ANN (VMAP) to efficiently implement $d$-wave supercurrent visualization, achieving imaging of supercurrent speeds $V(r)$ at magnetic fields $|B| \leq μT$ in $\mathrm{Bi_2Sr_2CaCu_2O_8}$. Correspondence between specific characteristics of $N(r,E)$ around each supercurrent loop and a quantum "Rosetta Stone" which translates $N(r,E)$ to $V(r)$, emphasizes the validity of $V(r)$ detection and visualization. Then, for hole-densities 0.17 $\leq p \leq$ 0.22 we observe statistically repeatable networks of supercurrent flows. Crucially, these supercurrents satisfy Kirchhoff's law at junctions within each network. Further, theoretical predictions for supercurrent speeds $V$ in disordered $d$-wave superconductors are consistent with measured 1250 m/s $< V <$ 4000 m/s, and with reported magnetic field amplitudes $|B| \approx$ 0.1 mT Thus, detection and visualization of these supercurrent loop networks provides unique perspectives on $\mathcal{T}$-symmetry breaking in cuprates. It also emphasizes the accelerating utility of ANN techniques for physics discovery from high data volume quantum matter research.

papers.abstract: Unconventional superconductivity in rhombohedral $n$-layer graphene exhibits a rich phase diagram with multiple distinct superconducting regions, whose microscopic origins remain unclear. Here, we investigate the competition between charge-density-wave (CDW) and pair-density-wave (PDW) instabilities near the inner van Hove singularities (VHSs), using a patch renormalization-group approach with the realistic band structures incorporated. We identify two key findings. First, we find an effective attractive interaction emerging from purely repulsive interactions through RG flow in the presence of $C_3$ symmetry breaking. The resulting interaction structure, with two repulsive couplings and one attractive coupling, gives rise to competing CDW and PDW instabilities. Second, the competition is controlled by the detuning from the VHS. While CDW dominates near the VHS filling and at higher temperatures, PDW becomes the leading instability on either side of the VHS and at lower temperatures. This mechanism naturally produces two superconducting regions separated by a CDW-dominated regime, providing a possible qualitative explanation for the experimentally observed separation between SC1 and SC2.

papers.summary: Kiessling, Altshuler and Yuzbashyan conjectured the thermodynamic transition picture for the isotropic Eliashberg spin-chain functional with vanishing Coulomb pseudopotential: the normal state is the unique minimizer above and at a critical temperature, the superconducting minimizer below it is unique up to gauge, and the transition is continuous. papers.abstract: Kiessling, Altshuler and Yuzbashyan conjectured the thermodynamic transition picture for the isotropic Eliashberg spin-chain functional with vanishing Coulomb pseudopotential: the normal state is the unique minimizer above and at a critical temperature, the superconducting minimizer below it is unique up to gauge, and the transition is continuous. We establish the nonlinear part of this picture. In the variables $ρ_n=\sin^2θ_n$, the condensation energy restricted to the first quadrant is strictly convex, and folding any admissible chain into that quadrant cannot increase its energy. For every positive, non-increasing interaction with power-law decay, hidden convexity and a compactness estimate give existence and uniqueness of the minimizer up to gauge. The normal state minimizes the energy exactly when its quadratic form is non-negative, including marginal stability. Among admissible chains, a positive solution of the nonlinear Eliashberg equations exists exactly when the normal state is linearly unstable and is then unique. For temperature-dependent families with pointwise continuity and locally uniform decay bounds, the minimizing density is continuous in a weighted $\ell^1$ norm. Together with uniqueness of the linear-stability temperature, these results prove the thermodynamic conjectures for the $γ$-model, Einstein phonons and general phonon spectra; the phonon applications use separately established spectral input. Finite-dimensional algebraic and convex-analytic components are machine-checked in Lean. The proofs were obtained independently of concurrent work that reaches overlapping conclusions.

papers.abstract: Phase-incoherent preformed excitons have long been anticipated in excitonic insulators, yet their characteristic signatures and underlying physics remain elusive, as the electrical neutrality of excitons hinders direct probes of condensate phase coherence. Here we exploit the emergent excitonic density wave driven by phase-coherent pairings in systems hosting momentum-separated electron and hole Fermi pockets, such as monolayer 1$T'$-MoTe$_2$, as an experimentally accessible probe of excitonic phase coherence. We observe in 1$T'$-MoTe$_2$ that the density-wave order and its associated emergent collective excitations, as revealed by Raman spectroscopy, vanish above $T_c\approx80~$K, whereas the excitonic-insulator state, characterized by a single-particle gap in transport and tunneling measurements, persists up to $T_g\approx100~$K, revealing an intermediate pseudogap-like regime of preformed excitons without long-range phase coherence. Theoretically, we attribute this intriguing separation to two distinct processes governing the loss of excitonic order by its own emergent excitations: boson-driven phase decoherence and fermion-driven pair breaking. Specifically, we identify an emergent low-lying collective excitation as a lattice-pinned phason (phase mode), whose heating-induced gap softening enhances phase fluctuations and drives condensate phase decoherence above $T_c$, while thermal excitations of fermionic quasiparticles gradually suppress and ultimately destroy pairing amplitude at the higher $T_g$. The self-consistent microscopic calculation quantitatively captures our key observations, establishing an excitonic realization of preformed-pairing physics.

The calculation identifies a low-lying collective excitation as a lattice-pinned phason whose thermally softened gap enhances phase fluctuations and destroys phase coherence above the lower transition. Thermal fermionic quasiparticles, in turn, gradually weaken and ultimately destroy the pairing amplitude at the higher temperature; the authors report that the calculation quantitatively captures the key observations.
papers.result_zh: 密度波序及其相关集体激发的 Raman 信号在约 80 K 以上消失，而由输运和隧穿中的单粒子能隙表征的激子绝缘体状态可持续至约 100 K。作者将这一温度区间解释为缺乏长程相位相干的预形成激子赝能隙区间。计算将一种低能集体激发识别为受晶格钉扎的 phason，其能隙随升温软化并增强相位涨落，从而在较低转变温度以上破坏相位相干。另一方面，热激发的费米子准粒子会逐渐削弱并最终破坏较高温度下的配对振幅；作者称计算定量再现了关键观测。
papers.future_en: Independent phase-sensitive probes across the approximately 80–100 K interval could further test whether the gap persists without long-range coherence. Measurements that track the proposed phason softening and pairing amplitude with temperature would help distinguish the two loss processes described by the calculation.
papers.future_zh: 在约 80–100 K 区间开展独立的相位敏感测量，可进一步检验能隙是否在缺乏长程相干时仍然存在。随温度追踪所提出的 phason 软化与配对振幅，有助于区分计算描述的两种序消失过程。
papers.tier_reason_en: The abstract presents a potentially important separation between the loss of excitonic phase coherence near 80 K and the persistence of an excitonic gap to about 100 K, supported by multiple probes and a microscopic account. This combination of an experimentally accessible preformed-exciton regime and a quantitative framework is strong enough to merit a high-tier assessment.
papers.tier_reason_zh: 摘要提出了一个具有潜在重要性的温度分离：激子相位相干性在约 80 K 附近消失，而激子能隙持续至约 100 K；这一结论由多种测量和微观理论支持。实验可探测的预形成激子区间与定量理论框架相结合，足以支持较高档次的评价。

papers.abstract: The normal state of cuprate superconductors is believed to host precursor electron pairing above the superconducting transition temperature. These pre-formed pairs, which extend over an unknown temperature range, are expected to lack long-range phase coherence. Because spectroscopic evidence for this hypothesis is only indirect, new methods to probe these physics are needed. Nonlinear terahertz spectroscopy allows one to probe high-order time correlation functions and is therefore sensitive to fluctuations. Measurements of third-harmonic generation along the superconducting planes have revealed responses persisting above Tc, but a clear relation between these optical responses and specific properties of the fluctuating state has not yet been established. Here, we apply angle-resolved multidimensional terahertz spectroscopy to probe the optical nonlinearity of the Josephson tunneling resonance in La1.83Sr0.17CuO4 across the superconducting to normal state transition. We find that among all third-order nonlinear responses, the non-rephasing multidimensional signal is especially sensitive to non-mean field fluctuations of the order parameter. We measure a crossover occurring at T ~ Tc between a mean-field optical nonlinearity that dominates at low temperatures and one that is mediated by short-range superconducting fluctuations. We present a theoretical framework that connects the out-of-plane optical response in both regimes to the fluctuating in-plane superconducting state, and contrast the sensitivity of different types of terahertz nonlinearities to fluctuating order.
papers.physics_advance: The non-rephasing multidimensional terahertz signal is especially sensitive to non-mean-field superconducting fluctuations, and its temperature dependence reveals a crossover near Tc from mean-field response to fluctuation-mediated response.
papers.relevance_reason: This is a strong cuprate superconductivity study that experimentally connects a nonlinear terahertz response to short-range order-parameter fluctuations and supports the interpretation with theory.
papers.summary_zh: 作者利用角分辨多维太赫兹光谱，研究 La₁.₈₃Sr₀.₁₇CuO₄ 跨越超导转变时的 Josephson 隧穿共振。他们报告，在 Tc 附近，光学非线性响应从低温下占主导的平均场响应转向由短程超导涨落介导的响应。
papers.method_en: The study measures angle-resolved multidimensional terahertz nonlinearities, including third-order responses, of the out-of-plane Josephson tunneling resonance across the superconducting-to-normal transition. A theoretical framework relates the out-of-plane optical response to fluctuations of the in-plane superconducting state.
papers.method_zh: 研究测量超导态到正常态转变过程中，面外 Josephson 隧穿共振的角分辨多维太赫兹非线性响应，包括三阶响应。作者建立理论框架，将面外光学响应与面内超导态的涨落联系起来。
papers.result_en: Among the measured third-order nonlinear responses, the non-rephasing multidimensional signal is reported to be especially sensitive to non-mean-field order-parameter fluctuations. The authors identify a crossover at approximately Tc: mean-field optical nonlinearity dominates at low temperature, while short-range superconducting fluctuations mediate the response above the crossover. Their framework connects the out-of-plane optical measurements in both regimes to the fluctuating in-plane superconducting state. The work therefore proposes a more specific spectroscopic probe of precursor pairing than a nonlinear response whose relation to the fluctuating state is not established.
papers.result_zh: 在测得的三阶非线性响应中，作者报告非重聚焦多维信号对非平均场序参量涨落尤其敏感。他们在约 Tc 处识别出一个交叉：低温下平均场光学非线性占主导，而交叉以上的响应由短程超导涨落介导。其理论框架将两个温区的面外光学测量与面内超导态涨落联系起来。因此，该研究提出了一种比与涨落态关系尚未明确的非线性响应更具针对性的前驱配对光谱探测方法。
papers.future_en: Measurements across a broader temperature range could establish how the non-rephasing signal evolves above Tc and delimit the fluctuation-mediated regime. Comparing this response with other terahertz nonlinearities and testing the theoretical link to in-plane fluctuations would further clarify its diagnostic specificity.
papers.future_zh: 在更宽温度范围内开展测量，可确定非重聚焦信号在 Tc 以上的演变，并界定涨落介导区间。将该响应与其他太赫兹非线性进行比较，并检验其与面内涨落的理论联系，可进一步厘清其诊断特异性。
papers.tier_reason_en: The work combines a multidimensional nonlinear spectroscopic measurement with a framework that relates a selected signal to superconducting fluctuations, addressing an important but difficult-to-probe regime above Tc. The abstract supports a focused and potentially influential result, while providing limited evidence for the broader reach expected at higher tiers.
papers.tier_reason_zh: 该研究将多维非线性光谱测量与理论框架相结合，把一种特定信号联系到超导涨落，针对的是 Tc 以上重要但难以探测的区域。摘要支持其为一项聚焦且可能有影响力的结果，但对更高档次所需的广泛影响力提供的证据有限。

papers.title: From a High-T$\rm_C$ Spin-Gapless Semiconductor to a Spin-Glass: The Role of Disorder in NiMnCrAl

papers.summary_en: This study examines how chemical disorder changes the predicted spin-gapless-semiconducting and ferrimagnetic behavior of the Heusler alloy NiMnCrAl. The measured material instead displays glassy magnetism and metallic transport.

papers.abstract: We combine first-principles calculations with structural, magnetic, and transport measurements to investigate the influence of chemical disorder on the quaternary Heusler alloy NiMnCrAl. For the ordered Y-type structure, density-functional-theory calculations predict a ferrimagnetic spin-gapless-semiconducting state with a total magnetic moment of $1.99\,μ_{\mathrm{B}}/\mathrm{f.u.}$ and a mean-field ordering temperature of approximately $1300~\mathrm{K}$. Polycrystalline NiMnCrAl forms in a single average cubic phase; however, combined x-ray diffraction, neutron diffraction, and extended x-ray absorption fine-structure measurements reveal substantial antisite disorder, characterized by predominantly B2-like disorder with additional cross-sublattice mixing. No long-range ferrimagnetic transition is observed up to $700~\mathrm{K}$. Instead, the compound exhibits a broad magnetic anomaly near $37~\mathrm{K}$, frequency-dependent ac susceptibility, slow stretched-exponential relaxation, and field-cooled and zero-field-cooled memory effects, establishing a glassy magnetic state. The electrical resistivity is metallic and the Seebeck coefficient is negative, consistent with the loss of the ideal spin-gapless electronic structure. Exchange-interaction calculations show that antisite disorder introduces short Mn--Mn separations and competing antiferromagnetic Mn--Mn and Mn--Cr interactions, providing a microscopic basis for magnetic frustration. These results demonstrate the strong sensitivity to the predicted spin-gapless and ferrimagnetic states of NiMnCrAl to chemical disorder.
papers.physics_advance: Antisite disorder in NiMnCrAl suppresses the predicted long-range ferrimagnetic, spin-gapless state and produces a spin glass, with competing Mn–Mn and Mn–Cr interactions providing a microscopic basis for the frustration.
papers.relevance_reason: This combines magnetic and transport measurements with first-principles and exchange calculations to establish how chemical disorder frustrates magnetism in a quantum material.
papers.summary_zh: 本文研究化学无序如何改变 Heusler 合金 NiMnCrAl 预测的自旋无隙半导体与亚铁磁行为。实验材料则表现出玻璃态磁性和金属输运特征。
papers.method_en: The authors combine first-principles calculations with structural, magnetic, and transport measurements. X-ray and neutron diffraction and extended x-ray absorption fine structure are used to characterize disorder, while exchange-interaction calculations examine its magnetic consequences.
papers.method_zh: 作者结合第一性原理计算以及结构、磁性和输运测量。研究利用 X 射线与中子衍射、扩展 X 射线吸收精细结构表征无序，并通过交换相互作用计算考察其磁学后果。
papers.result_en: For the ordered Y-type structure, calculations predict a ferrimagnetic spin-gapless state with a moment of 1.99 μB/f.u. and a mean-field ordering temperature of approximately 1300 K, whereas the disordered polycrystal shows no long-range ferrimagnetic transition up to 700 K and exhibits a glassy anomaly near 37 K. Predominantly B2-like antisite disorder with additional cross-sublattice mixing is associated with competing antiferromagnetic Mn–Mn and Mn–Cr interactions; the resistivity is metallic and the Seebeck coefficient is negative.
papers.result_zh: 对于有序 Y 型结构，计算预测其为亚铁磁自旋无隙态，磁矩为 1.99 μB/f.u.，平均场有序温度约为 1300 K；而无序多晶样品在 700 K 以下未出现长程亚铁磁转变，并在约 37 K 出现玻璃态磁异常。以 B2 型为主、并伴有跨子晶格混排的反位无序与 Mn–Mn 和 Mn–Cr 之间竞争的反铁磁相互作用相关；样品电阻率呈金属性，Seebeck 系数为负。
papers.future_en: The findings motivate further investigation of whether reducing antisite disorder can recover the predicted spin-gapless and ferrimagnetic states. The abstract does not specify a particular follow-up experiment.
papers.future_zh: 这些发现促使人们进一步研究减少反位无序能否恢复预测的自旋无隙态与亚铁磁态。摘要未指定具体的后续实验。
papers.tier_reason_en: The work combines first-principles predictions with multiple complementary probes of chemical disorder and glassy magnetism, and provides a specific exchange-interaction-based account of the contrast between ideal and disordered material. Its focused study of one alloy and the absence of a demonstrated broadly applicable advance make PRB/Physical Review Materials an appropriate tier.
papers.tier_reason_zh: 该研究将第一性原理预测与多种互补手段结合，用于考察化学无序和玻璃态磁性，并基于交换相互作用解释理想结构与无序材料之间的差异。其研究聚焦于单一合金，且未展示广泛适用的突破，因此 PRB/Physical Review Materials 是合适的层级。

papers.authors: Coline Thevenard, Carenza E. Cronshaw, Romain Tahay, Daria Gusakova, Vincent Baltz, Richard F. L. Evans
papers.summary_en: The study reports ultrafast laser-pulse imprinting of antiferromagnetic skyrmions in a coupled ferromagnetic/antiferromagnetic bilayer and examines how a magnetic field affects nucleation.

papers.abstract: Antiferromagnetic skyrmions are promising topologically protected entities for robust storage and THz transport of information. Their generation has so far relied on slow techniques or on specific magnetic structures, which limit their integration into spintronic devices. Here, we demonstrate the imprinting of antiferromagnetic skyrmions within a few picoseconds in a coupled ferromagnetic/antiferromagnetic bilayer with a thermal laser pulse. We identify a threshold energy required to initiate the fused skyrmion phase and show that this can be modulated by a magnetic field, enabling deterministic nucleation of antiferromagnetic skyrmions. Compared to conventional slow field-cooling processes to control antiferromagnets we show that laser-induced skyrmion imprinting can be orders of magnitude faster and provides an experimentally feasible route towards ultrafast creation and manipulation of antiferromagnetic skyrmions.
papers.physics_advance: A thermal laser pulse can imprint antiferromagnetic skyrmions in a few picoseconds; their nucleation has an energy threshold that can be tuned with magnetic field.
papers.relevance_reason: The experiment establishes ultrafast nucleation and field control of antiferromagnetic skyrmions in a coupled magnetic bilayer, a substantive result in quantum magnetism.
papers.summary_zh: 该研究报告了通过超快激光脉冲在铁磁/反铁磁耦合双层中印刻反铁磁斯格明子，并考察磁场对成核的影响。
papers.method_en: The authors investigate skyrmion formation following a thermal laser pulse in the coupled bilayer, identifying the initiation threshold and varying the magnetic field to control nucleation.
papers.method_zh: 作者研究耦合双层受到热激光脉冲后的斯格明子形成过程，确定其启动阈值，并通过改变磁场控制成核。
papers.result_en: Antiferromagnetic skyrmions are imprinted within a few picoseconds, and the authors identify a threshold energy for initiating the fused-skyrmion phase. They report that a magnetic field can modulate this threshold and enable deterministic nucleation; the process is described as orders of magnitude faster than conventional slow field-cooling.
papers.result_zh: 反铁磁斯格明子可在数皮秒内被印刻，作者还确定了启动融合斯格明子相所需的阈值能量。他们报告磁场能够调节该阈值并实现确定性成核；这一过程被描述为比传统缓慢场冷快数个数量级。
papers.future_en: Further work could test the proposed laser-driven nucleation route experimentally and assess its controllability in device-relevant bilayers, as suggested by the stated motivation.
papers.future_zh: 后续研究可对所提出的激光驱动成核路径进行实验检验，并评估其在器件相关双层中的可控性，这与本文提出的研究动机一致。
papers.tier_reason_en: Picosecond-scale, field-controlled nucleation would be a meaningful advance for antiferromagnetic textures, but the abstract gives limited methodological detail and does not establish whether the demonstration is experimental; a specialist materials/condensed-matter tier is the best-supported assessment.
papers.tier_reason_zh: 皮秒尺度且可由磁场控制的成核对反铁磁磁结构而言具有实质意义；但摘要的方法细节有限，也未明确说明该演示是否为实验结果，因此专业材料或凝聚态物理期刊档次是最有依据的评估。

papers.announcement_time_basis: arXiv dated batch and official 20:00 Eastern release schedule
papers.authors: Guo-Jian Qiao, Zhi-Lei Zhang, C. P. Sun
papers.summary_en: The paper introduces a real-space landscape index for inhomogeneous chiral systems and establishes its relation to protected chiral zero modes at interfaces.
papers.summary: We define a real-space topological index from the geometry of a quadratic landscape associated with the spatial dynamics, which is governed by the zero-energy eigenvalue equation of chiral systems. The landscape index remains invariant under continuous deformations preserving the uniform exponential separation between decaying and growing spatial solutions and equals the continuum winding number i
papers.abstract: We define a real-space topological index from the geometry of a quadratic landscape associated with the spatial dynamics, which is governed by the zero-energy eigenvalue equation of chiral systems. The landscape index remains invariant under continuous deformations preserving the uniform exponential separation between decaying and growing spatial solutions and equals the continuum winding number in the homogeneous limit. Across an inhomogeneous interface, the difference between the indices on the two sides equals the protected net chiral zero-mode count, without requiring asymptotically homogeneous bulk regions. Explicit landscape constructions yield analytical bounds on Hamiltonian parameters and their spatial gradients that determine the indices for all profiles satisfying these bounds, without specifying their detailed spatial form. Dimensional reduction extends the landscape index and its boundary correspondence to higher-dimensional systems. The resulting bounds guarantee protected radial zero modes in effective Kitaev-type systems of arbitrary transverse codimension and identify parameter and momentum regions supporting chiral edge states in periodically modulated quantum anomalous Hall systems. For the quasiperiodic interface considered, the index difference guarantees a single protected chiral branch despite persistent modulation on both sides, as confirmed by numerical calculations. Landscape geometry thus connects real-space topology to the protected net chirality of boundary states.
papers.physics_advance: A real-space landscape index remains invariant for inhomogeneous chiral systems and its interface difference counts protected net chiral zero modes, even without asymptotically homogeneous bulk regions.
papers.relevance_reason: This develops a theoretical topological classification for inhomogeneous electronic and Bogoliubov-de Gennes systems and derives protected boundary-state predictions.
papers.summary_zh: 本文为非均匀手征系统引入实空间景观指标，并确立该指标与界面受保护手征零模之间的关系。
papers.method_en: The authors define the index from the geometry of a quadratic landscape associated with the zero-energy equation, prove its invariance under a uniform exponential separation condition, and extend the construction through dimensional reduction.
papers.method_zh: 作者根据与零能方程相关的二次景观几何定义该指标，证明在均匀指数分离条件下其保持不变，并通过降维将构造推广到更高维系统。
papers.result_en: The index reduces to the continuum winding number in the homogeneous limit, and its difference across an inhomogeneous interface equals the protected net chiral zero-mode count without requiring asymptotically homogeneous bulks. The work also derives profile-independent parameter and gradient bounds, and applies them to Kitaev-type systems, periodically modulated quantum anomalous Hall systems, and a quasiperiodic interface where the index difference guarantees a single protected chiral branch.
papers.result_zh: 在均匀极限下，该指标退化为连续体系的绕数；而在非均匀界面两侧，指标之差等于受保护手征零模的净数目，无需假设体区渐近均匀。该工作还推导了与具体空间剖面无关的参数及梯度界，并将其应用于 Kitaev 型系统、周期调制量子反常霍尔系统，以及指标差保证存在单条受保护手征支的准周期界面。
papers.future_en: Further work could investigate how the landscape-index bounds can be used to characterize additional inhomogeneous chiral systems and boundary-state regimes beyond the examples treated here.
papers.future_zh: 后续研究可探讨如何利用景观指标的界限，刻画本文示例之外的其他非均匀手征系统及其边界态区域。
papers.tier_reason_en: The abstract presents a broad and mathematically substantial real-space index with a boundary correspondence that does not require homogeneous bulks, plus several applications; the claims support a strong specialist theory paper, while no evidence here establishes a wider-than-field impact.
papers.tier_reason_zh: 摘要提出了适用范围较广且数学内容扎实的实空间指标，并给出无需均匀体区的边界对应关系及多项应用；这些结果支持其成为有力的专业理论论文，但摘要未显示超出该领域的影响证据。
